top_level_objectives: Identify the major structural components of the DNA double helix, including sugar-phosphate backbones, nitrogenous bases, and hydrogen bonds.
Explain antiparallel strand orientation using 5' to 3' and 3' to 5' directionality.
Apply complementary base-pairing rules to predict paired bases and hydrogen-bond patterns.
Describe the roles of helicase, single-strand binding proteins, DNA polymerase, and DNA ligase during DNA replication.
Explain why leading- and lagging-strand synthesis differ and how this follows from DNA polymerase directionality.
Interpret semiconservative replication as producing daughter DNA molecules with one parental and one newly synthesized strand.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce DNA as a three-dimensional double helix and orient students to its overall geometry before focusing on molecular details.
key_visuals: A large rotating DNA double helix suspended in front of the student
Two differently colored outer strands winding around a shared central axis
Inward-facing paired bases forming rungs across the helix
student_actions: Walk around or rotate the model to view the helix from the side and down the central axis
Identify the outer backbones and inner base-pair region using simple labels
Note that both strands spiral around the same axis rather than forming separate ladders

scenes.brief_purpose: Focus on the chemical parts of DNA and the specificity of complementary base pairing.
key_visuals: Zoomed-in section of DNA showing sugar, phosphate, and base components
Color-coded bases labeled A, T, G, and C
Hydrogen bonds shown as dashed lines, with two between A–T and three between G–C
student_actions: Tap labeled molecular parts to distinguish sugars, phosphates, bases, and hydrogen bonds
Match free bases to exposed partners according to A–T and G–C rules
Compare the number of hydrogen bonds in A–T versus G–C pairs

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how 5' and 3' ends define strand direction and why the two DNA strands run antiparallel.
key_visuals: One DNA segment partially straightened with arrows along each sugar-phosphate backbone
Clear 5' and 3' labels at opposite ends of each strand
A highlighted sugar-phosphate chain showing direction from one nucleotide to the next
student_actions: Trace each backbone from 5' to 3' using gesture prompts
Place or confirm 5' and 3' labels on both strands
Explain from the arrows why one strand runs opposite the other

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the start of replication by showing helicase separating parental strands and stabilizing proteins binding exposed templates.
key_visuals: A replication fork forming in the DNA helix
Helicase positioned at the fork, unwinding base pairs
Single-strand binding proteins attached along the separated parental strands
student_actions: Activate helicase to unwind a short region of DNA
Observe hydrogen bonds breaking while covalent backbones remain intact
Place or recognize single-strand binding proteins on exposed single-stranded DNA

scenes.scene_name: Scene 5: DNA Polymerase and 5' to 3' Synthesis
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect polymerase activity to strand directionality by showing that new DNA is extended only at the 3' end.
key_visuals: Parental template strands with free complementary nucleotides nearby
DNA polymerase adding nucleotides to a growing strand
A directional arrow indicating new-strand synthesis in the 5' to 3' direction
student_actions: Add complementary nucleotides to a template strand in the correct order
Identify the growing 3' end where DNA polymerase can extend
Reject or correct an attempted addition at the 5' end to reinforce polymerase directionality

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how antiparallel templates create continuous leading-strand synthesis and discontinuous lagging-strand synthesis.
key_visuals: A moving replication fork with one new strand extending continuously toward the fork
Short Okazaki fragments forming away from the fork on the opposite template
Directional arrows contrasting leading and lagging synthesis
student_actions: Predict which template supports continuous synthesis based on its orientation
Trigger polymerase movement on the leading strand and then on lagging-strand fragments
Arrange Okazaki fragments in the order they are made as the fork advances

scenes.scene_name: Scene 7: Joining Fragments and Completing Replication
scenes.brief_purpose: Show maturation of the lagging strand and summarize the production of two daughter DNA molecules.
key_visuals: DNA ligase sealing gaps between adjacent Okazaki fragments
Two completed double helices separating from the replication region
Parental strands colored differently from newly synthesized strands
student_actions: Use ligase to join Okazaki fragments into a continuous strand
Inspect each daughter molecule to identify old and new strands
State why each final DNA molecule is semiconservative
